one_line: A human-controlled studio for authoring and rendering fictional coding-agent sessions.
what_it_does: Lets an agent write structured scripts for chat or terminal scenes while a person reviews, edits, previews, and exports deterministic SVG/video output.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools expose timeline, camera, frame snapshots, validation, proposals, and export against live stage state; generic UI driving would be materially less precise and repeatable.
leverage_evidence: About text lists 13 site tools including load_script, inspect_timeline, snapshot_frame, fit_duration, propose_patch, approval, and export.
Transcript says the agent reads the guide, loads a script, changes a choice/theme, inspects the stage, and exports animated SVG.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent studio workflow from authoring through playback and export, with approval and undo concepts; frame sheets visibly show the dark workspace, script/stage states, and agent rail, though small text limits verification.
execution_evidence: Transcript describes script load, camera, playback, choice, voice input, theme changes, and SVG export.
Three frame sheets show a consistent multi-pane stage/editor interface across workflow states.
Devpost screenshot shows a named submission and embedded demo.
impact_rationale: It addresses a concrete need for safe, repeatable, re-shootable demos for READMEs, documentation, talks, and posts without leaking real session secrets.
impact_evidence: About text explicitly identifies READMEs, docs, talks, and posts as users and use cases.
Privacy default, approval of rewrites/exports, and deterministic rendering are claimed.
creativity_rationale: The fictional coding-agent-session format and agent-on-stage/human-at-controls interaction is a fresh, memorable use of WebMCP beyond ordinary app automation.
creativity_evidence: Pitch frames the product as a studio for fictional coding-agent sessions.
Transcript demonstrates branching choices, voice input, scene direction, and terminal/app surfaces.
usability_note: Clear staged workflow and visible agent rail; dense studio controls may require learning.
standouts: Strong shared-state authoring and inspection model.
Deterministic export and privacy-aware fictional sessions.
advance_reason: High WebMCP delta with coherent demonstrated workflow and distinctive creative concept.

one_line: A human-approval layer for agent-proposed fixes on a live web page.
what_it_does: Scans accessibility, SEO, and performance, highlights live elements, stages evidence-backed patches, waits for approval, then reapplies and rescans.
leverage_rationale: The agent and human share live DOM targets and a typed approval-gated mutation loop; screenshots or generic UI automation would be less reliable for evidence and safe staged changes.
leverage_evidence: About text describes scan_page, highlight_issue, propose_fix, apply_fix with unresolved approval, revert_fix, and export_patch.
Frame sheets visibly show issue lists, highlighted elements, proposed fixes, and Approve/Skip controls.
execution_rationale: The packet gives a complete scan-propose-approve-apply-rescan loop and frames show its major states, but the claimed 23-change end state is not independently observed.
execution_evidence: Claims 54 to 100 overall and 100/100/100 per pack after 23 approved changes.
Screenshots show issue inventory, agent working state, fix draft, and approval sheet.
Devpost packaging identifies the live-page approval product.
impact_rationale: Accessibility, SEO, and performance remediation are real recurring problems, and the product directly addresses unsafe unattended edits with reviewable changes.
impact_evidence: Bundled fixture has 23 issues across accessibility, SEO, and performance.
Evidence cards and no-guessing behavior target accountable remediation.
creativity_rationale: Human approval as a live-page WebMCP primitive and refusing to invent human-facing content is a thoughtful synthesis, though the audit/remediation category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: apply_fix remains pending until a visible human click.
propose_fix requires agent-authored text for ambiguous human-facing fields.
usability_note: Issue grouping, highlighting, and explicit approval make the workflow understandable.
red_flags: No submitted video despite frame-sheet references; visual evidence is packaging/demo montage rather than a verified recording.
standouts: Shared live-element targeting with evidence-backed patches.
advance_reason: Clear agent-native remediation loop with strong practical value and substantial WebMCP leverage.

one_line: An accessible-by-default browser IDE that lets agents edit, preview, and audit front-end projects together.
what_it_does: Combines Monaco multi-file editing, live preview, WCAG auditing, responsive checks, design-token enforcement, and WebMCP agent access.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP can give an agent structured access to editor, preview, and audit state in one tab, reducing handoffs, but a capable general agent could reproduce much of the workflow with browser/devtools automation.
leverage_evidence: About text claims editor, preview, audit, and AI share one live tab.
WebMCP is described as closing the edit-preview-audit loop.
execution_rationale: The feature set is broad and plausible, but the submitted video is an unrelated Rick Astley music video and no gallery images are supplied, so core workflow completion is not evidenced.
execution_evidence: About text specifies multi-file editing, live preview, pour/WCAG audit, device preview, design tokens, and compatibility checks.
FACTS report video title as an unrelated official music video and gallery_images=0.
impact_rationale: Front-end teams and agent-assisted builders have a clear problem: accessibility and design-system quality are often lost during rapid coding; the integrated audit directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Project narrative identifies editor/dev server/browser/a11y-checker handoff friction.
Claims every preview refresh runs WCAG and best-practice checks.
creativity_rationale: Integrating live coding with continuous accessibility and design-token enforcement is a useful, ambitious synthesis, though the IDE category is established.
creativity_evidence: DESIGN.md treated as source of truth and drift flagged in AI-written CSS.
Accessibility is positioned as part of the authoring loop rather than a separate checker.
usability_note: Potentially powerful single-tab workflow, but no trustworthy visual demo is provided.
red_flags: Submitted video title is an unrelated Rick Astley music video.
No public repository and no gallery images; central claims cannot be checked from packet evidence.
standouts: Accessibility and design-system checks integrated into editing.
advance_reason: Promising concept, but the unrelated video leaves execution and eligibility insufficiently evidenced.

one_line: A live traffic-signal simulation where humans and agents search and safely commit intersection timings together.
what_it_does: Runs a San Francisco junction simulation in-tab, exposes structured batch evaluation and policy-enforced commit tools, and explains legal versus illegal timing tradeoffs.
leverage_rationale: The meaningful simulation state exists only in the page and is inaccessible to screenshots; structured tools enable hundreds of precise physics evaluations while keeping commit policy separate.
leverage_evidence: About text says a conventional browser agent cannot read mean_wait_s from pixels and would manage about five experiments versus 200 with tools.
run_batch evaluates candidates while apply_config alone commits and enforces constraints.
execution_rationale: The design is coherent and the packet gives specific simulation behavior and policy semantics, but no video is submitted and only one gallery image limits end-to-end observation.
execution_evidence: Specific reported values: best permissive-left 27.4s but prohibited; best legal timing 45.8s.
FACTS show alive demo, public repo, and one gallery image.
Narrative describes scrubbable explanations and live operator controls.
impact_rationale: Traffic engineers, educators, and planners can use a concrete sandbox to explore signal timing and understand safety/legal tradeoffs; the scenario has credible operational and learning value.
impact_evidence: Four-arm signalized junction models demand, timing, mean wait, and phasing constraints.
Human locks and commit policy preserve operator judgment.
creativity_rationale: Separating unconstrained physics discovery from constrained deployment is a subtle and memorable interaction design, not merely an agent wrapper around sliders.
creativity_evidence: The packet explicitly emphasizes run_batch versus apply_config as a design argument.
Agent searches off-main-thread while traffic continues and operator supervises.
usability_note: The separation of experiment and commit is legible, though domain concepts are specialized.
red_flags: No submitted video; end-to-end interaction is claimed rather than shown.
advance_reason: The strongest leverage case in the packet, with a technically and ethically thoughtful simulation workflow.

one_line: A privacy-preserving apparel store that lets a user's agent shop with private fit and trip context.
what_it_does: Searches and compares products, finds variants and sizes, builds a family/trip cart, and proposes checkout without storing the shopper's profile.
leverage_rationale: Semantic commerce tools let an external agent use private context and shared cart state without DOM clicking or retailer-held profiles; this changes privacy and repeatability materially.
leverage_evidence: About text says the agent sends constraints, never the profile, and the store learns only needed product constraints.
Tools include search_products, filter_products, find_matching_variants, compare_products, get_size_guide, add_to_cart, and propose_cart.
execution_rationale: The scenario and tool surface are coherent, with a live demo and public repo, but no video and only one gallery image limit observed proof of the full family-shopping flow.
execution_evidence: Pitch and narrative specify a seven-day Hawaii planning scenario.
FACTS show public repo, alive demo, and one gallery image.
Look Book is described as created by the agent.
impact_rationale: Online apparel shopping has real friction around sizing, family coordination, trip constraints, and privacy; the proposed agent/store split addresses those pain points directly.
impact_evidence: Narrative identifies repeated re-entry or permanent storage of sizes/preferences as the problem.
Shared cart and destination-aware product planning fit the stated scenario.
creativity_rationale: The zero-knowledge retail framing and agent-knows-you/store-knows-products boundary is a strong, memorable commerce interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Retailer has no intelligence of its own; external agent uses private context.
Family shopping without registering family members is a distinctive privacy design.
usability_note: Semantic shopping and proposed-cart review should reduce tedious filtering, though checkout behavior is not shown.
red_flags: No submitted video; full shopping and checkout loop is not visually verified.
standouts: Clear privacy boundary between agent context and retailer state.
advance_reason: High-value privacy-native commerce concept with a credible WebMCP delta.

one_line: SOUND Buoy lets people teach, review, and repair the operating context an autonomous web agent relies on.
what_it_does: Captures human feedback and project facts, exposes grounded context to agents, and supports review/correction of what the agent understood.
leverage_rationale: A browser-native context governance surface can ground agents in project-specific facts and corrections, but the packet does not establish that generic external memory or UI automation could not provide similar value.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly targets human-anchored context governance and repair via WebMCP.
Devpost evidence lists dark/light home pages and agent-feedback capture screens.
execution_rationale: The packet contains a substantial concept and screenshots, but no video frames were submitted and the about text is partially malformed/repetitive, limiting evidence of a complete workflow.
execution_evidence: FACTS say no frame sheets and no video.
Devpost screenshot set has four gallery images showing home and feedback capture states.
Description claims teach/review/approve/correct behavior but does not evidence end-to-end completion.
impact_rationale: Agents acting on stale, misunderstood, or unapproved project context create real operational risk; a human correction layer has credible value for teams using autonomous agents.
impact_evidence: Pitch names context grounding, human constraints, brand identity, and repair as recurring failure modes.
Project is framed as a browser-native reference point for moving work environments.
creativity_rationale: The buoy metaphor and focus on context repair rather than just tool execution is a fresh agent-infrastructure angle, though the actual interaction depth is unclear.
creativity_evidence: Human-anchored governance and repair is the central concept.
Feedback capture is shown in both dark and light modes.
usability_note: The metaphor and feedback capture appear approachable, but workflow completeness and access requirements are unclear.
red_flags: Packet text is malformed/repetitive in places and does not clearly establish the complete tool workflow.
standouts: Focuses on repairing agent context, not only exposing actions.
advance_reason: Interesting agent-governance premise, but evidence is too thin to advance confidently.

one_line: An asymmetric co-op game where humans guide a blindfolded AI player to smash a watermelon.
what_it_does: Gives the AI movement, orientation, proprioception, and social-listening tools while humans provide incomplete and potentially conflicting visual guidance.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the AI player's body and sensory/action boundary; replacing it with generic UI driving would undermine the deliberately asymmetric game design.
leverage_evidence: Five tools are the AI's turn, walk, swing, self-status, and guide-listening body/perception surface.
Tools intentionally withhold target coordinates, obstacle map, and correct guide, making the agent a genuine player.
execution_rationale: The rules, state separation, and tool constraints are clearly designed, with a live demo and frame sheet, but no video limits evidence of a completed playable loop.
execution_evidence: About text describes collision evidence, trust updates, cautious movement, and swinging decisions.
FACTS show alive demo and one gallery image; frame sheets show the game evidence but small UI details are limited.
impact_rationale: It offers credible entertainment and a memorable way to explore human-agent collaboration, trust, and asymmetric capabilities, even if the audience is niche.
impact_evidence: Narrative gives a clear co-op premise where neither human nor AI can win alone.
Guide Chorus introduces social ambiguity and trust reasoning.
creativity_rationale: The human-eyes/AI-body split, deliberately blind agent, and conflicting human testimony create a novel interaction model pursued deeply through game mechanics.
creativity_evidence: Design principle is explicitly 'Physical clarity, social ambiguity.'
AI is an actual player rather than assistant, NPC, or game master.
usability_note: Simple physical tools and human guidance are accessible; conflicting testimony may create intentional challenge.
red_flags: No submitted video; playability and complete win state are not directly demonstrated.
standouts: WebMCP is intrinsic to the game mechanic, not an added control panel.
Trust and testimony make collaboration mechanically meaningful.
advance_reason: Exceptionally creative and genuinely agent-native game concept with high WebMCP indispensability.

one_line: A mutual-prediction game where humans and agents choose and block image-associated words together or against each other.
what_it_does: Uses shared image perception and WebMCP participation for solo and team modes, requiring prediction, blocking, coordination, and unpredictability.
leverage_rationale: The agent is a participant with its own choices and shared game state, making structured turns more reliable than generic UI driving, though the action space is relatively bounded.
leverage_evidence: About text says the agent is playing rather than powering the interface.
Game supports solo human-versus-agent and team human-plus-agent modes with coordinated choices.
execution_rationale: The rules and modes are coherent and gallery/frame evidence shows multiple game states, but there is no video or direct end-to-end result proof.
execution_evidence: Narrative clearly explains word choice, prediction, blocking, scoring, solo, and team modes.
FACTS show alive demo, public repo, and three gallery images.
Frame sheets show repeated game UI states.
impact_rationale: The game provides entertainment and a useful low-stakes way to observe and learn agent collaboration, but its practical audience/problem fit is narrower than utility products.
impact_evidence: About text explicitly positions it as a game and as a way to observe how agents perceive and coordinate.
Team mode supports shared human-agent play.
creativity_rationale: Turning agent perception and prediction into a symmetric/asymmetric game with solo and team variants is a fresh interaction model for WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: The agent is designed as a participant and opponent, not an interface backend.
Rules avoid reaction-speed and logic advantages by centering intuition/perception.
usability_note: Finite word choices and clear modes should be approachable; strategy may take explanation.
red_flags: No submitted video; complete multiplayer/team flow is claimed rather than directly shown.
standouts: Team mode makes complementary human and agent perception explicit.
advance_reason: Distinctive, coherent agent-participant game with meaningful WebMCP use.

one_line: A human-approved continuity ledger that reconciles stale business facts before agents publish or transact.
what_it_does: Recovers conflicting records, keeps provenance, lets humans approve or reject claims, publishes a draft passport, and prepares qualified inquiries without granting agents publish authority.
leverage_rationale: Typed browser tools expose bounded conflicts and source-backed proposals while preserving visible human authority; generic scraping or clicking would tend to collapse provenance and miss the safety boundary.
leverage_evidence: About text describes Recover → Reconcile → Approve → Publish → Transact and a Continuity Ledger with source separation.
Agent has no accept/publish tool; only visible human controls can publish.
execution_rationale: The packet articulates a coherent provenance and approval workflow with a concrete coffee-supplier scenario, but no video and no gallery images reduce direct verification.
execution_evidence: Four specific disagreements are named: phone, minimum order, Japan availability, and certification claim.
Draft Passport admits only accepted facts and preserves unresolved claims.
FACTS show public repo and alive demo but zero gallery images.
impact_rationale: Businesses and their agents need current, qualified, source-backed information; preventing stale claims from reaching customers or transactions is a credible operational benefit.
impact_evidence: Narrative gives concrete consequences of stale phone, order, export, and certification information.
The fictional Ugandan coffee supplier demonstrates a realistic continuity case.
creativity_rationale: The continuity ledger and publish-authority separation are a thoughtful, memorable reframing of agent readiness as information governance rather than mere scraping.
creativity_evidence: Agent-ready stale information is explicitly rejected as the thesis.
Source-backed proposals, unresolved claims, and human-only publishing are central mechanics.
usability_note: Five visible stages provide a clear mental model, though reconciliation may be domain-heavy.
red_flags: No video or gallery images; end-to-end behavior is narrative-only in this packet.
advance_reason: Strong real-world value and careful agent/human authority design despite limited visual evidence.

one_line: A browser brick CAD workspace where humans and agents co-edit a validated, undoable 3D model.
what_it_does: Searches a large brick catalog, places and transforms modeled parts, checks connectors/collisions/constraints, previews ghost edits, and shares revision-aware state with agents.
leverage_rationale: Agents receive structured CAD geometry, connectors, revisions, selection, validation, and dry-run results rather than screenshots; generic UI driving cannot comparably provide reliable geometric editing and preflight.
leverage_evidence: Transcript explicitly contrasts WebMCP structured state with screenshots and describes exact document revision, selection, validation summary, and shared connector logic.
build_preflight dry-runs batches through the same CAD kernel, including collision, connectivity, protected regions, and constraints.
execution_rationale: The video transcript and frame sheets evidence a broad but coherent end-to-end CAD workflow with catalog search, live 3D edits, validation, ghost preview, undo, and rendering; demo_alive is unknown, so confidence is not maximal.
execution_evidence: Transcript shows a model transformed to gothic style through agent tool calls and inspected from another angle.
It describes 80,000 indexed identities, 900 modeled placeable parts, and shared manual/agent connector logic.
Frame sheets visibly show consistent 3D building workspace and agent/tool activity; Devpost screenshot packages the demo.
impact_rationale: Brick builders, designers, educators, and hobbyists gain a real editable design partner that handles repetitive geometry while preserving human creative control.
impact_evidence: Narrative identifies the limitation of AI outputs that require manual reconstruction and the need for real connections/orientations.
Features include editable models, real parts, connection checks, subassemblies, and undo.
creativity_rationale: Applying agent-native collaboration to physically constrained brick CAD, with a shared geometric kernel and human/agent consequences, is highly original and ambitious.
creativity_evidence: Agent can transform an existing six-story building into gothic architecture in the shared model.
Catalog identity/placeability distinctions and preflight ghost edits show deep pursuit of the concept.
usability_note: Manual drag/drop plus agent edits and undo make the collaboration legible, though CAD complexity is inherent.
red_flags: Demo availability is marked unknown in FACTS.
standouts: Best evidence of structured state changing a creative workflow.
Shared CAD kernel, validation, revisions, and undo unify human and agent actions.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage and execution evidence with a deeply pursued, memorable creative collaboration model.
